nodes.name: analyze_agent.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline station 6 that performs deep LLM-based analysis of enriched news items, generating structured JSON with headline, summary, key numbers, winners/losers, geo angles, and confidence scores, using a YAML SOP file to guide domain-specific prompting.

nodes.name: analyze_item
nodes.summary: Performs LLM-based analysis of a single enriched news item by constructing a prompt from clean text, extracted entities, enrichment data, and domain SOP, then retries up to 3 times to get valid JSON output.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main entry point for the analyze pipeline stage; fetches all analyze-pending items from the database, calls analyze_item for each, and writes structured analysis results back to the analyzed_items table.

nodes.name: validate_analysis_output
nodes.summary: Validates LLM analysis JSON output for required fields and correct data types, emitting warnings on validation failures.

nodes.name: classify_agent.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline station 3 that assigns domain tags, geo tags, and importance scores to extracted news items using heuristics over entity data, source credibility weights, and geographic mappings.

nodes.name: compute_importance_score
nodes.summary: Computes a 0-1 importance score for a news item by weighting source credibility, entity count, and keyword signals extracted from the classification payload.

nodes.name: parse_geo_tags
nodes.summary: Extracts and normalizes geographic tags (country and region) from entity data in extracted items, mapping country names to geo regions.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main classify stage entry point; processes all extracted items to compute importance scores, domain tags, and geo tags, then persists classified_items rows.

nodes.name: clean_agent.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline station 1 (post-ingest) that strips HTML, removes boilerplate, detects language, deduplicates using SHA-256 hashing and sentence-transformer embeddings, and normalizes raw news text.

nodes.name: is_duplicate
nodes.summary: Detects duplicate news items using a two-pass check: exact SHA-256 hash match on the first 500 chars, then cosine similarity via sentence-transformer embeddings against a rolling window of recent items.

nodes.name: clean_item
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full cleaning pipeline for a single raw item: HTML stripping, boilerplate removal, normalization, language detection, duplicate checking, and word count enforcement.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main clean stage entry point; fetches all unprocessed raw items, applies clean_item to each, and writes passing items to the cleaned_items table.

nodes.name: enrich_agent.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline station 4 that enriches classified news items with real-time financial data from Yahoo Finance (stocks, commodities) and macroeconomic indicators from the FRED API, with TTL-based caching in SQLite.

nodes.name: fetch_stock_data
nodes.summary: Fetches 5-day stock price history via yfinance for a given ticker symbol, computing current price, 5-day change percent, market cap, and P/E ratio, with SQLite-backed TTL caching.

nodes.name: fetch_fred_data
nodes.summary: Fetches macroeconomic time series (CPI, unemployment, GDP, federal funds rate, VIX) from the FRED API and caches results in SQLite.

nodes.name: enrich_item
nodes.summary: Enriches a single classified item by resolving mentioned company names to ticker symbols and fetching their stock data, plus commodities and FRED macro indicators.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main enrich stage entry point; fetches all classified items, calls enrich_item for each, and writes enrichment results to enriched_items table.

nodes.name: extract_agent.py
nodes.summary: Pipeline station 2 that uses the Gemini LLM to extract structured fields (headline, summary, entities, sectors, sentiment, key_number) from cleaned news text using a file-based prompt template.

nodes.name: extract_item
nodes.summary: Calls the LLM with a structured extraction prompt for a single cleaned item, with up to 3 retries, and validates JSON output against required fields.

nodes.name: run

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The replit.md README is the authoritative project document: it describes the 8-station AI pipeline (Ingest → Clean → Extract → Classify → Enrich → Analyze → Format → Quality Gate), every API endpoint, all required environment variables, and the Replit deployment workflow. Start here to understand what NewsLens is — a multi-agent news intelligence platform that converts raw RSS, Reddit, and Substack feeds into structured 'impact cards' — before diving into the code that implements it.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: main.py is the FastAPI application bootstrap: it registers the cards, user, and sources route routers under the /api prefix, wires up CORS middleware, initializes the database, seeds demo cards, and starts the APScheduler pipeline on startup. Everything the README describes flows outward from this single file — reading it gives you the complete runtime wiring of the backend before you explore any individual component.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's lifespan context manager (the @asynccontextmanager pattern) replaces the deprecated @app.on_event('startup') approach. It runs setup code before yield and teardown code after, ensuring the scheduler and database are initialized before the first request is served.

tour.title: Central Configuration
tour.description: settings.py is the single source of truth for all runtime constants: API keys for Gemini, Reddit, and FRED; the SQLite database path; the LLM model and endpoint; pipeline schedule interval; enrichment cache TTL; and source credibility weights. With a fan-in of 12 — the fourth-highest in the codebase — virtually every backend module imports from here, making it the connective tissue that binds the pipeline together.
tour.languageLesson: Python's os.getenv with a default value is the idiomatic pattern for reading environment variables: os.getenv('KEY', 'default'). The .env.example file documents all required variables with placeholder values, serving as both onboarding guide and contract between the runtime environment and the code.

tour.title: News Sources Configuration
tour.description: sources.yaml declares all 22 ingestion sources — 10 RSS feeds, 9 subreddits, and 3 Substack newsletters — each tagged with domain (Finance, Tech, Geopolitics, Environment), geographic region, and a credibility rating. This file is the data-plane configuration for Station 1 of the pipeline; changing which sources NewsLens monitors requires only editing this YAML, not the ingest agent code.

tour.title: Pipeline Orchestrator
tour.description: orchestrator.py sequences all 8 pipeline stages into a single run_pipeline function and registers it with APScheduler for periodic automatic execution. This is the highest-level view of the pipeline logic: it calls each agent in order (ingest, clean, extract, classify, enrich, analyze, format, quality_gate), records results in the pipeline_runs table, and handles stage-level error isolation so a failure in one station does not abort subsequent ones.

tour.title: Ingest Agents: RSS, Reddit, Substack
tour.description: The three ingest agents each implement Station 1 of the pipeline for a different source type: rss_agent.py uses feedparser to consume RSS/Atom feeds, reddit_agent.py uses PRAW to fetch hot posts and top comments from subreddits, and substack_agent.py reads Substack newsletter RSS feeds. All three deduplicate by URL or external_id and write new articles into the raw_items table, providing the raw material for every subsequent station.

tour.title: Database Schema: The 6-Stage Progression
tour.description: schema.sql defines the complete SQLite data model: six tables that mirror each pipeline station (raw_items → clean_items → extracted_items → classified_items → enriched_items → cards), plus three supporting tables (user_profiles, swipe_events, pipeline_runs) and an enrichment_cache. Understanding this schema reveals the pipeline's state machine — each row advances through tables as it is processed, and the cards table is the final published output consumed by the API.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite's WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode, enabled here in database.py, allows concurrent reads while a write is in progress — critical for a pipeline that writes data while the API simultaneously reads the cards table. The database.py fetchone/fetchall/execute helpers wrap connection management so callers never handle commit/rollback directly.

tour.title: Stations 2-4: Clean, Extract, Classify
tour.description: These three agents form the structural processing core. clean_agent.py (Station 2) strips HTML, detects language, and deduplicates using SHA-256 hashing and sentence-transformer embeddings. extract_agent.py (Station 3) sends cleaned text to the Gemini LLM using the extract.txt prompt template to pull out entities, event type, geography, sector, and a confidence score. classify_agent.py (Station 4) then applies rule-based heuristics over the extracted data to assign domain/geo tags and an importance score.

tour.title: LLM Prompt Templates
tour.description: The extract.txt and analyze.txt prompt files are the textual contracts that govern what the Gemini LLM produces at Stations 3 and 6. extract.txt instructs the model to return a JSON object with entities, event type, geography, sectors, and confidence. analyze.txt drives the deep impact analysis: winners/losers with quantified magnitude, country-specific angles (India, USA, China), and an optional personalized impact section. These files are the clearest expression of NewsLens's differentiating value — quantified, structured news analysis.
tour.languageLesson: File-based prompt templates (loaded via open().read() at runtime) make it easy to iterate on LLM behavior without touching Python code. The sop.yaml provides the domain-specific rules (magnitude anchors, time horizons, geo angle templates) that the analyze prompt references, separating 'what to ask' from 'how to judge the answer'.

tour.title: Stations 5-6: Enrich & Analyze
tour.description: enrich_agent.py (Station 5) fetches real-time financial context — live stock prices from Yahoo Finance (yfinance), commodity data, and macroeconomic indicators from the FRED API — and caches results in the enrichment_cache table with a TTL. analyze_agent.py (Station 6) then combines the enriched context with the cleaned article to call the Gemini LLM via the centralized llm_client.py, producing the structured winners/losers/angles JSON that defines the final card content.

tour.title: Stations 7-8: Format & Quality Gate
tour.description: format_agent.py (Station 7) assembles the final card row by joining data from all prior stages — extraction, classification, enrichment, and analysis — into the unified schema required by the cards table. quality_gate.py (Station 8) then evaluates each candidate card against thresholds: minimum summary length, presence of winners/losers, confidence score floor, and key number presence. Only cards passing all checks are marked live=true, making them visible to the frontend API.

tour.title: API Routes: Cards, Users, Sources
tour.description: The three route files implement the REST surface that the frontend consumes. cards.py handles filtered card listing, personalized card ranking by user sector profile, single card retrieval, and swipe event recording. user.py provides profile upsert and retrieval. sources.py exposes source status monitoring and a manual pipeline trigger endpoint. All routes are described by the Pydantic models in api/models.py, which enforce request/response schemas throughout.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI uses Pydantic models for both request validation and response serialization. Declaring a response_model= on a route endpoint means FastAPI will validate and filter the response to match the model schema, giving you automatic OpenAPI documentation and type safety with no extra code.

tour.title: OpenAPI Contract & Code Generation
tour.description: openapi.yaml is the machine-readable contract for the entire NewsLens API — 9 endpoints and 13 component schemas. The orval.config.ts in lib/api-spec drives two code-generation targets from this single YAML: a TanStack React Query client in lib/api-client-react (typed hooks like useListCards, useSwipeCard) and a Zod validation library in lib/api-zod (auto-generated TypeScript types and schemas). This pattern means the frontend never manually writes API types — they are generated from the authoritative spec.
tour.languageLesson: OpenAPI-driven code generation (via orval here) eliminates the 'type drift' problem where frontend types fall out of sync with backend responses. The pattern is: define the contract once in YAML, regenerate clients on every schema change, and let TypeScript's compiler catch mismatches at build time.

tour.title: React Frontend: App Shell & Routing
tour.description: main.tsx mounts the React app, and App.tsx wires up the providers — React Query for server state, TooltipProvider, and Wouter for client-side routing — then declares routes mapping paths to Feed, CardDetail, Sources, Profile, Pipeline, and SavedCards pages. The api.ts facade re-exports all generated React Query hooks from the api-client-react library so no page component ever imports directly from the generated code, keeping the abstraction layer clean.

tour.title: The Swipe Card UI
tour.description: NLSwipeCard.tsx is the core user interaction surface — it renders a news impact card with domain badges, confidence scores, winners/losers summaries, and swipe action buttons, then dispatches swipe events to the backend via the recordSwipe API call. The useSwipeGesture.ts hook tracks pointer and touch events to detect horizontal swipes and animate the card, while useKeyboardShortcuts.ts adds arrow-key navigation. NLCardDetail.tsx provides the full detail view with tabs for Summary, Sources, and Analysis when a card is tapped.
tour.languageLesson: Custom hooks like useSwipeGesture encapsulate imperative DOM event logic (addEventListener, pointer capture) behind a clean React interface that returns declarative state (direction, offset, isAnimating). This separates gesture detection from rendering, making the card component purely concerned with display.
